name: Street Corn Chicken Rice Bowl

ingredients.buy: 2/3 cup crumbled; 1/2 cup crumbled, for topping
juice and zest of 3 1/2 limes; 7 tablespoons
1/2 cup chopped; 2/3 cup chopped; 1 1/2 cups leaves, for topping

writer_notes: Ingredient-vs-step audit passed both directions: all 20 locked lines are used, no step uses anything unbought.
Sea Salt has two amounts (chicken rub + rice) and a separate 'Salt' line covers the corn salad's scant teaspoon; I kept these as distinct uses in the steps to match the buy strings.

No cost_lines were in this dispatch, only per-serving macros, so shop_smart deliberately makes no per-ounce or lasts-N-batches claims. All cost prose uses the ${{cost_ps}} token plus the $1/month membership line.
Source offered 'pickled OR fresh red onions'; only fresh Red Onion was purchased, so I wrote fresh red onion and did NOT add a pickling step (no pickling ingredients were bought).
Hero macros written as {{cal}}/{{protein}} tokens; bounds ('under 800 calories', 'at least 40 g protein') stated literally against the run band.
Jalapeno kept as optional per the transcription and locked buy string.

prose.intro_html:
Mexican street corn is one of those things people happily pay six bucks for at a fair, then eat standing up over a napkin. We are going to put it in a container with seasoned chicken and cilantro lime rice, and eat it all week for a fraction of that. This is a street corn chicken rice bowl, and it is built for the fridge.

The math here is friendly. Every bowl lands at 597 calories with 44.6 grams of protein, which means you get the creamy, tangy, cheesy payoff of elote alongside a serving of chicken that actually keeps you full until the next meal. No sad diet plate energy. Just a real dinner that happens to be cheap and happens to hit its numbers.
prose.shop_smart:
• The chicken is the whole ballgame at 4 3/4 pounds of boneless skinless breast. Buy it in the largest family pack the case has rather than the little foam trays up front, and cut it into 1-inch chunks yourself. Chunks cook faster and season on every side.
  • Canned corn is your friend here. You need 7 cups drained, so grab whole-kernel cans and drain them well before they hit the yogurt. Frozen corn works too if you thaw and pat it dry first, but canned is the no-fuss path.
  • Cotija shows up twice, once folded into the corn salad and once crumbled on top, so pick up a block or a tub with enough for both. If your store is out, a firm queso fresco crumbles the same way.
  • You are buying limes for juice AND zest, so do not reach for the plastic squeeze bottle. Real limes give you both, and you need the zest for the rice and the salad.
  • Long-grain white rice is the base, 3 1/2 cups uncooked. The store-brand bag does exactly what the name-brand bag does. Same with the spice rack: chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder and onion powder are all pantry staples that pay you back across a lot of future batches.
  • Avocado and red onion are the fresh finish. Buy the avocados a touch firm so they last until you eat the last container, and cut them fresh each day if you can.
prose.make_it:
Start the rice. Bring the water to a boil in a medium pot, then stir in 3 1/2 cups long-grain white rice and the sea salt. Cover, drop the heat to low, and simmer about 20 minutes until the rice is tender. While it steams, stir together the chopped cilantro, fresh lime juice and lime zest in a bowl. When the rice is done, fold it into that cilantro lime mix while it is still warm so it drinks up the flavor.

Mix the street corn salad. In a big bowl, combine the drained corn, Greek yogurt, cotija, mayonnaise, lime juice and zest, the diced jalapeno if you want the heat, chopped cilantro and the scant teaspoon of salt. Stir it gently until it is creamy and coated, taste it, and adjust the salt or lime. Set it aside.

Season and sear the chicken. In a small bowl, stir together the chili powder, sea salt, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder and onion powder. Toss the chicken chunks in that spice blend until every piece is coated. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium, and once it shimmers add the chicken. Cook 4 to 5 minutes per side until it is cooked through and the center hits 165 degrees. Do not crowd the pan, work in two batches if you have to, because a crowded pan steams instead of sears.

Build the bowls. Spread warm cilantro lime rice across the bottom, top with chicken chunks, add a generous scoop of the street corn salad, then finish with cubed avocado, sliced red onion, a little more crumbled cotija, some cilantro leaves and a squeeze of lime.
prose.portion_html:
This is a build-and-weigh job, so it comes out even instead of eyeballed. Cook everything, then weigh your rice pot, your corn salad bowl and your cooked chicken separately, each minus the empty container weight. Take each number and divide by 14, and that is your per-bowl target for that component.

Line up all 14 containers and lay the rice down first, hitting its per-bowl weight, then the chicken, then a scoop of the corn salad to its number. That way container number 14 looks exactly like container number 1, and nobody gets the sad short-scoop at the end of the week. The avocado, red onion, extra cotija, cilantro and final squeeze of lime are best added the day you eat that bowl so the avocado stays green and the onion stays sharp.
prose.cost_closing_html:
Here is where the fairground math falls apart in your favor. A single street corn bowl from a fast-casual spot runs you double digits before tax and tip. This one lands at ${{cost_ps}} a serving, chicken and all, and you made 14 of them at once. That is not a coupon, that is a different way of buying dinner.

The chicken and the rice do the heavy lifting on cost, and every one of them clears {{protein}} grams of protein for under 800 calories. You are paying for groceries, not for a name on a paper bowl.
prose.upsell_html: Fourteen restaurant-style bowls, one afternoon, ${{cost_ps}} each. That is the Thrifty Crew way: eat like you are spending real money, spend like you are not. Every recipe, every price sheet and every batch plan lives behind the membership, and the membership is a dollar a month. One skipped bowl at the fair pays for the whole year.

head.description: Meal-prep Street Corn Chicken Rice Bowls: seasoned chicken, creamy Mexican street corn salad and cilantro lime rice, scaled to 14 high-protein containers under 800 calories.
head.keywords: street corn chicken bowl, mexican street corn rice bowl, meal prep chicken bowls, high protein meal prep, cilantro lime rice, elote chicken bowl, budget meal prep dinner
steps: Bring the water to a boil, add the rice and sea salt, cover and simmer on low about 20 minutes until tender. Stir chopped cilantro with lime juice and lime zest in a bowl, then fold the warm rice into it.

In a large bowl, combine the drained corn, Greek yogurt, cotija, mayonnaise, lime juice and zest, diced jalapeno if using, chopped cilantro and salt. Stir gently, taste and adjust the seasoning, then set aside.
In a small bowl, stir together the chili powder, sea salt, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder and onion powder. Toss the 1-inch chicken chunks in the spice blend until coated.

Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium. Add the chicken and cook 4 to 5 minutes per side until cooked through and the internal temperature reaches 165 degrees, working in batches so the pan is not crowded.

Spread warm cilantro lime rice in each container, top with chicken and a scoop of the street corn salad. Add cubed avocado, sliced red onion, crumbled cotija, cilantro and a squeeze of lime when you serve.
Weigh the rice, chicken and corn salad separately and divide each by 14 to get per-bowl targets, then portion evenly across all 14 containers.
